It is plain static files with no build step, so GitHub Pages can serve the repo root as-is: index.html loads style.css and app.js by relative path, and app.js imports the other two modules the same way, so a project site at username.github.io/efme/ works without any config. What was built

The app lives in [/Users/dreeves/lab/efme](/Users/dreeves/lab/efme) as static files with no build step or dependencies. Preview: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/933d53e3-3857-4aef-b0eb-87264a17d38e (a single-file bundle of the same sources).

  • [flowchart.js](flowchart.js) transcribes the chart as 40 nodes with answers (label, chart box color, target). Curly quotes, "Accomodate", "Look forward :", the "(see pg 2)" references, underscore counts, and bold/italic/underline spans are preserved as drawn.
  • [efme.js](efme.js) is the DOM-free walk (start, choose, back, atStart, current), asserting on every impossible input. [app.js](app.js) only renders the current node and wires buttons.
  • [quals/flowchart.qual.js](quals/flowchart.qual.js) holds the golden table (text with emphasis markers, colors, edges) plus structural quals: reachability, step badges, Perge routing, the node-merge rule, and a check that style.css styles exactly the kind and color vocabularies. [quals/efme.qual.js](quals/efme.qual.js) covers the walk. npm run qual runs 66, all green.
  • [style.css](style.css) is the candy treatment: glossy 3D pill buttons in the chart's box colors, a zigzag starburst halo behind the chart's star boxes, confetti on "Hell yeah, get started!", staggered entrances, reduced-motion support.
  • [reference/flowchart.png](reference/flowchart.png) is the 2048px source image (the largest Tumblr serves; no PDF or alt text exists).

Verification

A blind-transcription workflow (six agents reading image tiles without the data, diffs against the golden table, two adjudicators zooming on every difference, plus completeness, routing, and emphasis sweeps) found three real errors, all fixed: answers under step 2 and under PRIORITIZE were listed in the opposite order from the drawing, and the underline in step 5 runs through the space after "complete". A separate adversarial code review against AGENTS.md produced the fixes described above. Rendering was checked with headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths, including keyboard focus flow.

Decisions to know about

  • Ordering rule. Answers follow reading order as drawn: boxes whose vertical extents overlap read left to right, otherwise top to bottom. So step 2 now shows "No, that’s why I’m using this" before "Yes!", as the chart does.
  • Latin placeholders, each with a TODO comment: "Perge" (continue button on stars that say "Go to Step N"), "Retro" (back), "Ab initio" (start over). The credit label was changed by hand to "Source:" in the IDE, so it is treated as human copy and its TODO was removed; "jackalwedding · Tumblr" keeps a TODO as agent-composed attribution.
  • Not modeled. The "(cont'd from page 1)" connector boxes are pure pagination and are skipped. The four "Hell yeah, get started!" stars are one node; the two "Go to Step 4." stars and the two "Can the need be met" boxes stay separate because their arrows differ.
  • One unresolvable character. Trailing dots ("I still don’t know...") could be three periods or an ellipsis glyph; at this resolution they are indistinguishable, so three periods are used.
  • Double-click guard. A freshly rendered button is hidden and unclickable only during its stagger delay (120ms for the first), so a second click of a hasty double click lands on nothing without making the buttons feel laggy.
  • Node ids are vocabulary worth a glance: know, can-start, why-trouble, ten-minutes, why, tolerable, mindfulness, wellbeing, need-kind, need-met-emotional, prioritize, break-it-down, hell-yeah, interrupt-inertia, diy-dopamine, resist-impulses, go-to-4-protest, dbt-willfulness, please-4, fine, other-reasons, did-you-actually, complete-now, delegate, partially, worth-it, and the terminal stars.

Housekeeping: rule 15 is enforced in the global settings (every mutating git command is denied, plus a git-guard hook); this directory is not a git repository yet. A generated file, sourcery.html, appeared in the project directory during the session and was left untouched; it would be published along with everything else on GitHub Pages. On rule 10's question, the missing principle is "explicit over implicit", the anti-DWIM half of the Zen of Python.

The code review finished (96 agents). Cross-checking its final confirmed and split lists against the fixes already applied.

The review's final tally: 20 confirmed and 24 split findings, all already handled in the earlier fix batch, with 66 quals still green. Four low-severity items were left as they are on purpose:

  • The golden table's text normalization collapses repeated newlines, so a doubled <br> in the data would be invisible to it. The allowed-tag and typography quals still bound what the html can contain.
  • The data object is not deep-frozen; nothing in the app mutates it, and freezing 40 nested objects buys little.
  • The state stays a one-field record rather than a bare array, so a future field has a home.
  • The two CSS breakpoints stay unnamed; the base rules serve the middle range by design.

Nothing else is pending. The project directory, the 66 quals, and the published preview at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/933d53e3-3857-4aef-b0eb-87264a17d38e all reflect the final sources.

That found eight failures, all small footer text sitting on the most saturated band of the page gradient.

| Element | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "Based on" label | 2.12:1 | 6.45:1 |
| Footer links | 3.25:1 | 5.21:1 |
| Footnote asterisk | 3.83:1 | 6.02:1 |

The root cause was two accent colors chosen to look candy on a white card and then reused as text on the gradient. The palette now splits that job: the bright pink stays for fills and shadows, a darker berry carries text, and the purple darkened. I also removed the opacity fading from two footer lines, since dimming text is exactly what costs contrast; hierarchy there now comes from size and weight. Lowest measurement on the page is 5.16:1 against a 4.5 requirement.

Two things to know. quals/contrast.qual.js now recomputes all of this from style.css, including deriving the darkest possible ground by blending each blob over each gradient stop, so a future color change fails the quals rather than the users. And the title tooltip on the Beeminder link is not reachable by keyboard and is skipped by many screen readers, which is a property of title itself; your copy is intact, but that text is decoration rather than something everyone will get.

Worse-is-better here is "keep both, shrink the card." New Jersey style prizes simplicity of implementation and will trade away correctness to get it: change two numbers, add no new concept, accept that it still spills at the most extreme font settings. The container-query option is the MIT answer, buying full correctness with new machinery. Letting the card grow is the most *anti-magic* in the branch-minimising sense, since it deletes the entire square special case so star cards behave like every other card, but it costs the star shape on the short cards too, which is most of them.

It caught JavaScript that disagreed with its HTML and stopped immediately instead of limping onward. Teaching $() to tolerate a missing element would be silently fixing a bad input, would add a branch, and would not touch the actual cause. The next mismatch would then fail somewhere later and quieter.

The cause is deployment atomicity, not app code. HTML and JS are separate files with separate cache entries that must agree. The only real fix is a version query on the asset URLs so fresh HTML can only ever pull matching JS.

That fix needs a build step, and the repo deliberately has none. Serving is python3 -m http.server. A hand-bumped version string is worse than nothing, because it is a manual step that will be forgotten and will create false confidence.

A partial fix would not close the hole. The module graph is six JavaScript files plus the stylesheet, each with its own independently started ten minute clock. Cache-busting only app.js would still let a fresh app.js meet a stale [efme.js](efme.js).

So the exposure is a ten minute window, only for someone who had the page open across a deploy, only when that deploy changes the HTML and JS contract. Worth revisiting if a build step ever arrives for other reasons. Not worth introducing one for this.

Rewording the question instead was rejected because the answer label presupposes just as hard, so a question-only rewording is incomplete, and a full rewording spends source copy on all readers to serve four. Re-routing the dead ends through existing advice boxes was the runner-up but lands the emotional-need reader on a list offering "Body double with a friend", one card after they said social contact is unavailable.

One graft from that runner-up is worth deciding separately. Point "I'm worried I'll fail." at break-it-down, which is what Step 3 already gives to the same stated worry under PERFECTIONISM. No Pareto improvements exist here. Every fix spends a little fidelity to the drawn chart to buy a reader who can answer honestly, so this is one dial rather than a menu. The good news is it reduces to two independent yes or no calls, neither of which touches any code.

Call one, the honest button. Give did-you-actually a third answer that goes where the green one already goes. Buys: a reader who was offered nothing can say so and still reach Step 5. Costs: one extra button on a card all readers see, and a label you have to write.

Call two, the graft. Point "I'm worried I'll fail." at BREAK IT DOWN instead of the bare "Go to Step 4." star. Buys: that reader gets the same help Step 3 already gives the identical worry under PERFECTIONISM. Costs: deletes an arrow the artist drew, and orphans one of the two boxes reading "Go to Step 4.", so a qual that pairs them goes too.

| | must misreport to reach Step 5 | arrive at Step 4 offered nothing |
|---|---|---|
| change nothing | 4 | 4 |
| button only | 0 | 4 |
| graft only | 3 | 3 |
| both | 0 | 3 |

Three things make these cheaper than they look. Neither touches [app.js](app.js), since both are rows of data plus the matching golden table entry. The graft costs the reader no destination, because everything in the chart stays reachable from BREAK IT DOWN, verified by walking it. And the orphaned box does not vanish from the app, because its twin survives on the RESIST IMPULSES branch with identical text.

Recommendation is yes to the button, and the graft is genuinely optional. The button is the one that unblocks the person in distress, since three of the four bare routes are the wellbeing dead ends that no re-routing reaches. The graft only fixes the fourth route, and it is worth taking mainly because it is the one place the source contradicts itself, which makes correcting it the mildest editorial act available.

If you want the smallest possible commitment, take the button alone. That is one new line in [flowchart.js](flowchart.js), one in [quals/flowchart.qual.js](quals/flowchart.qual.js), and one new qual.
